app_subtitle: Smart crop finance for Indian farmers
schemes_header: Government Schemes You May Qualify For
why_cost_text: This estimate is based on average input costs (seed, fertilizer, labour, irrigation, and other expenses) for your crop, state, and season from government cultivation cost data. You can edit individual items above.
why_profit_text: Profit scenarios use historical yield and price data. Good harvest uses the 75th percentile, normal uses the median, and poor uses the 25th percentile for both yield and price. Actual results may vary.
why_breakeven_text: Break-even price is the minimum selling price needed to cover your total input costs, calculated as: Total Cost ÷ Expected Yield (quintals). Selling above this price means profit.
why_risk_text: Risk is measured using the Coefficient of Variation (CV) of historical yields and prices. Higher variation means higher risk. Green = low risk, Yellow = medium risk, Red = high risk.
why_dscr_text: The Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) compares your expected normal harvest income to your total loan repayment amount. A DSCR above 1.25 is considered safe; below 1.0 is a warning sign.
why_funding_gap_text: Funding gap = Total Cost − Own Capital. This is the amount you need to borrow. The KCC limit reduces this gap; any remaining amount is the residual gap you need to arrange separately.
why_lender_comparison_text: Interest is calculated using simple interest: Principal × Annual Rate × Months ÷ 12. The same formula is applied to all three lenders so only the rate differs. KCC rates are subsidized by the government.
why_msp_text: MSP (Minimum Support Price) is the government-guaranteed minimum price for your crop. If the market price falls below MSP, the government is supposed to procure at MSP. Selling above MSP is better.
scheme_kcc_desc: Low-interest revolving credit for crop inputs and allied activities. Eligible for all farmers with land ownership or lease documents.
scheme_pmkisan_desc: ₹6,000 per year direct income support in three installments of ₹2,000 each. Eligible for small and marginal farmers with cultivable land.
scheme_pmfby_desc: Subsidized crop insurance covering losses from natural calamities, pests, and diseases. Premium is 2% for Kharif and 1.5% for Rabi crops.
extra_moneylender_cost: Extra cost of moneylender vs KCC
error_rate_range: Moneylender rate must be between 1% and 100% per year.
